correctness.rationale: The group generators minus 1 are square-zero and their squarefree monomials are a basis. Linear-leading elements are images of a variable under a filtered automorphism and have rank 16. For Q=z1z2+z3z4, every monomial of degree at least three is divisible by one of the four derivatives of Q; successive substitutions starting at degree two produce the prescribed higher terms without changing earlier degrees. The homogeneous rank is (1+4+1) times 2. For Q=z1z2, normalize its coefficient by a unit, then shift z1 and z2 by the two coefficients in the square of the three-variable ideal. Their product vanishes by degree; this leaves Q+γz3z4z5 with γ measured by Q∧a3. For nonzero γ the tensor differential has homology dimension (4−2)(8−2)=12, giving rank 10 instead of 8. With cubic leading term, the top-degree output is already spanned by products with degree two; coefficients of degree four only add to that spanned output. The degree-four output has alternating rank 2 or 4, and the scalar input contributes one further dimension. Quartic/top leading terms give 2/1. Counting alternating forms by radicals and their nondegenerate quotients gives B2 and B4; the nonzero wedge functional has one fiber of size q^9 per value, and the free quartic and quintic coefficients contribute q^6. All counts sum to q^31. Independently, python3 /workspace/reproductions/rank.py used multiplication by XOR translation in the group basis for all 131203 higher-term choices on canonical nonlinear leading forms over F2, weighted by their leading orbits; the resulting binary counts agree term by term. The all-q argument is algebraic, not extrapolated from binary computation.

evidence: The all-algebra record covers arbitrary elements over every F_q of characteristic two; the only extra stratum is invertible multiplication.

Resultary 7cc1f8e3a451 gives the rank-8 versus rank-10 pair in dimension five, but its full census concerns four generators. Carlson et al. characterize flatness using independence modulo the radical square; Erdmann–Holloway identify support and rank varieties for truncated algebras.
